subject.title: iPhone Continuity Camera `--facing front` always uses rear camera

question: For macOS camera capture, should explicit `deviceId` remain the highest-precedence selector when `facing` is also provided for an iPhone Continuity Camera?
rationale: The current code makes `deviceId` an exact camera selector, but the reported user intent treats `facing` as an additional lens selector; automation cannot choose that contract without maintainer intent and live AVFoundation proof.

options.title: Preserve exact device targeting
options.body: Run live Continuity Camera proof first; if AVFoundation exposes no separate front selector, keep `deviceId` exact and document or surface a clear limitation.

options.title: Support Continuity lens remapping
options.body: If live proof shows a supported front/back selector for the same iPhone device, add a narrow macOS implementation with tests and docs.

options.title: Let facing override device id
options.body: Change selector precedence so `facing` can replace an explicit device id, accepting the compatibility risk for multi-camera users.

recommendation.title: Preserve exact device targeting
recommendation.body: Run live Continuity Camera proof first; if AVFoundation exposes no separate front selector, keep `deviceId` exact and document or surface a clear limitation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history across macOS camera capture, device-id support, and the prior closure of the related device-id feature request.
